revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Insulating Foam Order
revealWordProblem.text: The space station needs 3.8 meters of insulating foam to seal a hull panel. The foam costs $9.25 per meter. What is the total cost of the foam, and is your answer reasonable?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Multiply as whole numbers first: 38 × 925 = 35,150. Count decimal places: 3.8 has 1 and $9.25 has 2, for 3 total decimal places. Placing the point 3 places from the right gives 35.150, or $35.15. Check with an estimate: 4 × $9 = $36, which is close to $35.15, so the answer is reasonable.

vocabulary.termEs: Representar datos con diagramas de caja
vocabulary.definition: Show a data set's five-number summary in a box-and-whisker display.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Mostrar el resumen de cinco números de un conjunto de datos en un diagrama de caja y bigotes.
vocabulary.cloze: A box plot shows the ___-number summary: least, Q1, median, Q3, greatest.

examples.text: A box from Q1 75.5 to Q3 88 with whiskers to 68 and 94
examples.why: All five summary numbers are placed.

examples.text: A bar chart of the same scores
examples.why: Bars show counts, not quartiles.

vocabulary.definition: A graph that shows how data is spread using five key numbers.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una gráfica que muestra cómo se reparten los datos con cinco números clave.
vocabulary.visual: A box from Q1 to Q3 with a line at the median, and whiskers from min to max
vocabulary.cloze: A graph that shows data with a box and whiskers based on the five-number summary is a ___.

examples.text: A box holding the middle half, with whiskers to the extremes
examples.why: It displays the five-number summary.

examples.text: A line graph of scores over time
examples.why: That tracks change, not spread.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.
vocabulary.cloze: The middle value of the data, shown as a line inside the box, is the ___.

examples.why: The middle value once the numbers are in order.
Middle of an unsorted list is not the median.

vocabulary.definition: Numbers that split the data into four equal parts.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números que dividen los datos en cuatro partes iguales.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 → Q1 = 4 (median of lower half), Q3 = 12 (median of upper half)
vocabulary.cloze: A value that divides the data into four equal parts is a ___.

examples.why: It is the median OF that half.
That is the minimum, not a quartile.

vocabulary.definition: The spread of the middle half of the data (Q3 − Q1).
vocabulary.definitionEs: La extensión de la mitad central de los datos (Q3 − Q1).
vocabulary.visual: If Q1 = 12 and Q3 = 20, then IQR = 20 − 12 = 8 — the middle 50% spans 8 units
vocabulary.cloze: The distance between the first and third quartiles, showing the middle 50% of data, is the ___.

examples.why: Q3 minus Q1 — the middle half's width.
That is the range, using the extremes.

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: A box plot where the median is centered in the box shows symmetric distribution
vocabulary.cloze: The way data values are spread out is the ___.

examples.text: “Most scores cluster near 85, with one down at 68”
examples.why: It says where the data sits and how it spreads.
One value describes a point, not the shape of the set.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.visual: Small IQR = low variability in the middle 50%. Large IQR = high variability
vocabulary.cloze: How spread out the data values are is the ___.

examples.why: The values differ, which is what variability measures.
Nothing varies, so there is no spread to describe.

vocabulary.definition: Two numbers that describe spread: the range covers all the data, and the interquartile range covers only the middle half.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos números que describen la dispersión: el rango cubre todos los datos y el rango intercuartílico solo la mitad central.
vocabulary.visual: Range 26 covers 68 to 94; IQR 12.5 covers only 75.5 to 88
vocabulary.cloze: The range uses the ___ values; the interquartile range uses the ___.

examples.why: The IQR is always the smaller of the two — it sits inside the range.
The middle half cannot be wider than all of the data.

vocabulary.definition: Separate a multi-digit number into equal groups to find a quotient.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Separar un número de varias cifras en grupos iguales para hallar un cociente.
vocabulary.cloze: Long division repeats four steps: divide, multiply, subtract, ___ ___.

examples.why: The cycle runs until the last digit is used.

examples.text: Stopping at 12 with the 4 still waiting
examples.why: A digit left unused means the quotient is unfinished.

vocabulary.definition: Find a quotient with decimals by making the divisor a whole number first.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar un cociente con decimales convirtiendo primero el divisor en un número entero.
vocabulary.cloze: Make the ___ a whole number first, then move the dividend's point the same number of places.

examples.why: Both moved one place, so the quotient is unchanged.
Only the divisor moved, so the answer is ten times too small.

vocabulary.definition: The average of a data set. Add all the values, then divide by how many values there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio de un conjunto de datos. Suma todos los valores y divide entre cuántos valores hay.
vocabulary.visual: Miguel earned $60 in 4 days: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, so the mean is $15 per day.
vocabulary.cloze: The value found by adding all the data and dividing by how many values there are is the ___.

examples.why: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.
That is the total; the mean still needs the division.

vocabulary.definition: The average distance of data values from the mean; it describes spread.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia promedio de los valores de datos respecto a la media; describe la dispersión.
vocabulary.visual: MAD = sum of absolute distances from the mean ÷ number of values.
vocabulary.cloze: The average distance of each value from the mean is the ___.

examples.why: Absolute distances from the mean, then averaged.
Signed deviations always cancel — that is why they are made absolute.

vocabulary.definition: A mean, median, or mode chosen because it describes a data set fairly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una media, mediana o moda elegida porque describe un conjunto de datos de manera justa.
vocabulary.visual: Use the median when an outlier would pull the mean too far.
vocabulary.cloze: A center chosen because it describes the data fairly is an ___ ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Using the median when one salary is $40 million
examples.why: The outlier drags the mean; the median stays with the group.

examples.text: Using the mean in that same data set
examples.why: One extreme value pulls it away from every actual salary.

vocabulary.definition: Combine or find the difference between decimals by lining up equal place values.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Combinar o hallar la diferencia entre decimales alineando valores posicionales iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: Line up equal ___ ___ before you add or subtract decimals.

examples.why: Equal place values sit in the same column.

examples.text: 12.4 + 3.75 with the last digits lined up
examples.why: Aligning the ends puts tenths under hundredths.

vocabulary.definition: Find the product of decimals, then use place value to place the decimal point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar el producto de decimales y luego usar el valor posicional para colocar el punto decimal.
vocabulary.cloze: Count the decimal places in BOTH factors to place the ___ ___.

examples.why: One place plus two places is three places.
Only two places were counted, so the point landed too far right.

vocabulary.definition: The distance from the least value to the greatest value, found by subtracting: greatest − least.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia del valor menor al mayor, que se halla restando: mayor − menor.
vocabulary.cloze: Subtract the least value from the ___ value to find the range.

examples.why: Greatest minus least.
A range is a difference, never a sum.

vocabulary.definition: The number you are splitting up in a division problem.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número que estás repartiendo en una división.
vocabulary.visual: In 156 ÷ 12 = 13, the dividend is 156 — it is the total being split up
vocabulary.cloze: In 84 ÷ 7, the number 84 being divided is the ___.

examples.why: It is the amount being split.
That is the divisor.

vocabulary.definition: Another word for the mean — the amount each value would be if the total were shared equally.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Otra palabra para la media: la cantidad que tendría cada valor si el total se repartiera en partes iguales.
vocabulary.visual: A player averages 15 points per game, so over 10 games she scores 15 × 10 = 150 points in all.
vocabulary.cloze: A common everyday word that means the same thing as the mean is the ___.

examples.why: Total 44 shared equally across 4 values.
That is the total before sharing.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from the mean.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de la media.
vocabulary.visual: If mean = 20 and value = 17, deviation = 17 − 20 = −3 (3 below the mean)
vocabulary.cloze: How far a single value is from the mean is its ___.

examples.text: 7 being 3 away from a mean of 10
examples.why: It measures distance from the mean.
Deviation is measured from the mean, not another value.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.visual: 3.75 means 3 ones + 7 tenths + 5 hundredths — it is between 3 and 4
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show a value less than one whole is a ___.

examples.why: A part less than one, written after the point.
Without the point it is five wholes.

vocabulary.definition: The answer when you multiply.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La respuesta cuando multiplicas.
vocabulary.cloze: The answer to a multiplication problem is the ___.

examples.why: It is the result of multiplying.
That is a sum.

This catch-up station reviews Lessons 2.4–2.12: 2.4 Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot, 2.5 Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range, 2.6 Divide Multi-Digit Numbers Using an Algorithm, 2.7 Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm, 2.8 Describe Data Using the Mean, 2.9 Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation, 2.10 Choose Appropriate Measures, 2.11 Add and Subtract Decimals, 2.12 Multiply Decimals. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 2.4–2.12
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 2.4: The box always holds the middle 50% of the data, and the line inside the box is the median. • 2.5: Range = greatest − least, and it covers every value. Interquartile range = Q3 − Q1, and it covers only the middle half, so one faraway value cannot stretch it. • 2.6: Repeat the cycle Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down until no digits are left to bring down; what is left at the end is the remainder. • 2.7: Move the decimal point the same number of places in BOTH the divisor and the dividend, put the point in the quotient straight above it, then repeat Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down. • 2.8: Mean = total of all the values ÷ how many values there are. • 2.9: MAD = the average of how far each number is from the mean (always a positive distance). • 2.10: Use the mean for data with no outliers; use the median when an outlier or a skewed shape would pull the mean away from typical. • 2.11: Line up the decimal points, add zeros so each number has the same number of decimal places, then add or subtract one column at a time. • 2.12: Multiply like whole numbers, then the product has the SAME total of decimal places as both factors combined.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 2.4 — Represent and Describe Data in a Box Plot: The box always holds the middle 50% of the data, and the line inside the box is the median.

Lesson 2.5 — Describe Data by Range and Interquartile Range: Range = greatest − least, and it covers every value. Interquartile range = Q3 − Q1, and it covers only the middle half, so one faraway value cannot stretch it.

Lesson 2.6 — Divide Multi-Digit Numbers Using an Algorithm: Repeat the cycle Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down until no digits are left to bring down; what is left at the end is the remainder.

Lesson 2.7 — Divide Decimals Using an Algorithm: Move the decimal point the same number of places in BOTH the divisor and the dividend, put the point in the quotient straight above it, then repeat Divide → Multiply → Subtract → Bring Down.
Lesson 2.8 — Describe Data Using the Mean: Mean = total of all the values ÷ how many values there are.
Lesson 2.9 — Describe Data by Mean Absolute Deviation: MAD = the average of how far each number is from the mean (always a positive distance).
Lesson 2.10 — Choose Appropriate Measures: Use the mean for data with no outliers; use the median when an outlier or a skewed shape would pull the mean away from typical.
Lesson 2.11 — Add and Subtract Decimals: Line up the decimal points, add zeros so each number has the same number of decimal places, then add or subtract one column at a time.
Lesson 2.12 — Multiply Decimals: Multiply like whole numbers, then the product has the SAME total of decimal places as both factors combined.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 2.4: New, smaller data set: 2, 5, 5, 8, 11. First, what is the median (the middle value)?
From 2.5: Class A's box plot reads: least 62, Q1 74, median 81, Q3 87, greatest 90. Find the range first.
From 2.6: Let's do 384 ÷ 8. DIVIDE: 8 does not fit into 3, so we look at 38. How many 8s fit into 38? (4 — write it above the 8.)
From 2.7: Let's do 8.4 ÷ 2.1. STEP 0 — MOVE THE POINT: how many places make 2.1 a whole number? (1 place, so 2.1 becomes 21.)
From 2.8: New data set: a dog walker earns $9, $11, $16, and $12 over 4 days. First, what is the total?
From 2.9: New data set: 9, 10, 11. First, what is the mean? Add the three numbers and divide by 3.
From 2.10: Data set A: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Are there any outliers? If not, which measure should we use, mean or median?
From 2.11: Let's add 12.45 and 7.8. First, how do we write 7.8 with two decimal places? (7.80.)
From 2.12: Let's multiply 0.4 × 0.7. First multiply like whole numbers: what is 4 × 7? (28.)
